item.title: Is This Poker Player Bluffing? The AI Thinks So
item.description: ESPN unveiled an “AI tells detection” tool during broadcasts of the 2026 World Series of Poker. Is it a neat computer-powered party trick, or a real threat to poker’s future?

item.title: How One Startup Built a (Mostly) China-Free Robot
item.description: Ati Robotics assembles its robots in India and uses just a few Chinese parts—a strategy that could pay off as the Trump administration cracks down on Chinese humanoids.

item.title: ‘Everyone Is Doing It’: The Truth About AI in Hollywood
item.description: Puck’s Matthew Belloni says AI has quietly become part of everyday filmmaking. The battle now isn’t whether Hollywood will use the technology—it’s who controls what’ll come next.

item.title: How Data Centers Broke American Politics
item.description: What the Unabomber, Steve Bannon’s tech guy, and Bernie Sanders taught me about the great data center backlash of 2026.

item.title: Mistral Is in the Right Place at the Right Time
item.description: Open-weight AI models are having a moment in the wake of recent turmoil at US tech giants. For French AI lab Mistral, that’s the the best thing that could have happened.

item.title: Did an AI Music App Just Snitch on the Song of the Summer?
item.description: Fenix Flexin’s hit song “Rubberz” has hip-hop fans arguing over whether it was generated by AI. Some say they have proof it’s machine-made, but will anyone care?

item.title: AI Conquered Coding. Fast Food Is Next
item.description: Your next drive-thru order might be taken by a bot. And you might not even notice.

item.title: The ‘Guardrail Guy’ Went Viral for Posting About Flock Cameras. Then Someone Destroyed Them
item.description: Steve Eimers, also known as the “Guardrail Guy,” is done calling out license plate readers after two that appeared in his videos were vandalized.

item.title: Europeans Are About to Find Out How Entrenched AI Is in Their Daily Lives
item.description: New EU rules stipulate that people must be told when they’re interacting with AI or looking at AI-generated or -edited content, leading to fear of “disclosure fatigue.”

item.title: 7 States’ Water Systems Hit by Cyberattacks Likely Tied to Iran
item.description: Plus: The FBI eyes AI-powered tech to detect future crimes, Russia charges Telegram’s founder, xAI sues to stop a state’s “nudification” ban, and the Democrats learn a lesson about getting scammed.
